name: Steam Deck Controller (Composite)
notes: Issue #56, from PadForge discussion #337. The Valve-recognized Steam Deck persona: the real controller's vendor-page HID interface (06 FF FF, 64-byte input and feature reports) alongside the keyboard and mouse interfaces its lizard mode drives, at Valve's own 28DE:1205. Steam and SDL key Valve-device treatment on that identity plus this interface, which is why the plain steam-deck profile (a standard gamepad descriptor wearing the same ids) files under Generic DirectInput instead. Consumers drive the 64-byte Neptune report 0x09 frame through SubmitRawReport; Steam's haptic and rumble writes (0xEB, 0xEA, 0x8F) arrive as HID feature output on OutputReceived. The three report descriptors are verbatim from one physical Deck (hhd-dev/hwinfo steamdeck_lcd_v2, the same unit as its sd.pcapng USB capture); interface order, endpoint addresses, packet sizes and bIntervals are the real device's, from its lsusb -v dump. The real device also exposes a CDC ACM debug serial pair (interfaces 3 and 4) which this persona omits: it carries no controller data, and nothing in the input stack reads it.

reports.comment: ID_GET_ATTRIBUTES_VALUES. Verbatim from the real Deck's reply in the hhd-dev/hwinfo sd.pcapng capture, with the per-unit board/firmware identifiers kept as captured and ATTRIB_CONNECTION_INTERVAL_IN_US (0x0B) = 4000 us matching this persona's own 4 ms input cadence.
ID_GET_STRING_ATTRIBUTE, board serial. The real reply's framing with a HIDMaestro serial in place of the captured unit's.

layout.note: The persona's controller interface is an opaque 64-byte vendor blob, exactly as the real Steam Deck's is, so it declares no axes or buttons for a layout to reference. The Neptune report 0x09 frame the consumer submits through SubmitRawReport carries the full shape: two sticks, two trackpads, analog triggers, four back grips, and the 6-axis IMU. Same convention as the steam-controller profile, whose descriptor is also vendor-only.
